## Administrative information

- Amendment identifier: `002`
- Applies to: protocol version 1.0 and statistical analysis plan version 1.0
- Status: prospective, before production of the extended regional outputs
- Previous amendment: `001`

## Rationale

The initial analysis plan prespecified national, demographic and regional
descriptions. During development of the analytical figures, two additions were
identified as necessary for transparent reporting:

1. every figure should have an exact, machine-readable table containing the
   values used to construct it; and
2. national analyses should be reproduced at regional level whenever the
   source structure and compatible population denominators permit this.

These additions increase reproducibility and provide interested readers with
detailed supplementary results. They do not change the primary study question,
the primary pharmacological definition or the interpretation boundaries of the
study.

## Figure-data contract

Each generated figure will be linked to a figure-specific comma-separated
values file produced from the exact plotting dataset before graphical
rendering. Figure-data files will:

- retain unrounded analytical values whenever those values are available;
- contain the variables needed to reconstruct the plotted marks, grouping and
  facets;
- use stable filenames derived from the corresponding figure identifier;
- be listed in `output/tables/figure_data_manifest.csv`; and
- be made available as machine-readable supplementary material.

The report appendix will contain formatted versions of these tables or a clear
index to the machine-readable files when a table is too large for practical
page display. Formatting for publication may round displayed values, but the
linked comma-separated values files will remain the reconstruction source.

## Extended regional analyses

The extended regional appendix will reproduce national analyses at regional
level only where compatible numerators and denominators exist. Beneficiary
analyses remain restricted to 2020–2025 under amendment 001.

### Analyses to be produced

Subject to quality-control checks, the following will be produced for each
analysis region:

- annual class-level beneficiary counts and crude population rates;
- annual reimbursed boxes, reimbursement base and reimbursed expenditure;
- annual percentage and absolute changes;
- beneficiary counts and rates by sex and age group;
- age-sex-standardised regional rates using the prespecified standard
  population;
- regional ranks and summary measures of between-region variation;
- regional small multiples, heatmaps and maps where they improve
  interpretation; and
- figure-linked tables for every regional figure.

The main report will retain a limited set of regional headline results. The
full region-by-year and region-by-age-by-sex outputs will be placed in an
appendix or machine-readable supplement.

### Current feasibility limits

The following are not currently estimable from the ingested sources and will
not be inferred:

- regional class-level beneficiary measures for 2019;
- regional 2019 additive measures reconstructed from active-substance data;
  and
- regional active-substance composition unless a compatible official regional
  ATC5 source is added and validated.

Unknown or masked age, sex and region categories will remain excluded without
redistribution or imputation and will be reported in quality-control tables.

### Incomplete age-sex cells

Inspection before regional analysis showed that all absent primary age-sex
cells occurred in the 0–19-year age group. The following prospective rules
will be used:

- an observed primary cell will be analysed directly;
- an absent cell with no compatible unknown-age row for the same region, year
  and sex may be represented as a structural zero only when additive measures
  reconcile exactly with the direct regional source;
- an absent cell accompanied by a compatible unknown-age row will not be
  assigned a point estimate;
- point age-sex standardisation will require all six cells to be observed or
  supported structural zeros; and
- where an ambiguous cell prevents point standardisation, a conservative
  interval will be calculated by assigning between zero and all beneficiaries
  in the compatible unknown-age row to that cell.

These intervals describe uncertainty caused by disclosure control and are not
sampling confidence intervals. Unknown-age beneficiaries will not otherwise be
redistributed or imputed.

## Verification of 2025 regional data

Assurance Maladie reported an anomaly in the 2025 region-of-beneficiary data on
25 June 2026 and stated that it was corrected on 10 July 2026. Before any 2025
regional result is generated, the regional source files will be verified
against the corrected release using download metadata and SHA-256 checksums or
will be downloaded again from the official source.

Official notice:
[Assurance Maladie — Open Medic complete databases](https://www.assurance-maladie.ameli.fr/etudes-et-donnees/open-medic-base-complete-depenses-medicaments)

## Interpretation

Regional and demographic comparisons remain descriptive aggregate analyses.
They will not be interpreted as individual-level effects or causal estimates.
The large number of supplementary regional outputs is intended for transparent
description and hypothesis generation, not for confirmatory multiple testing.

## Consequences for versioning

Outputs created under this amendment will record:

- `amendment_id = "002"`; and
- an analysis version that identifies amendment 002.

Amendment 001 remains applicable to the historical ATC discontinuity and the
resulting analytical windows.
